name: comp-231
title: Searchable Timezone Select
description: A dropdown that lists timezones by GMT offset and place, with a search field on top to narrow it. Choosing a row closes the panel and puts that zone into the trigger.
use: When a settings form needs one timezone from the hundreds available and scrolling alone is too slow.
avoid: Labels are built from today's offset, so a zone's text shifts with daylight saving and cannot be fixed copy.
a11y: The trigger is a labelled combobox and typing filters the rows; the popover's open and close animation has no reduced-motion guard. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A small label sits above a wide rounded trigger reading a GMT offset plus a city, with a chevron at the right. Opened below is a dark panel whose top row is a search field, followed by tightly spaced rows of offset and place names.
behaves: Clicking the trigger opens the panel; typing in the search field filters the rows as you type, and picking one closes the panel and updates the trigger. The clip searches tok and ends on Asia/Tokyo.
customise: The starting zone and the field label are set in the file, while the rows are built from the browser's own timezone list at runtime. The search matching and offset formatting also live there.
weight: moderate: Builds, formats and sorts a label for every timezone in the browser list on mount.
